attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is complete for a purely local smooth-smeared core once composite Schwinger distributions exist, but it lacks a Yang-Mills theorem proving loop-space continuity and no reflection-plane boundary renormalization for Wilson-loop/cylinder observables produced by the RG construction.
steps: Fix a finite family F_1,...,F_N in the mirror-smooth positive-time core A_+^{ms} and coefficients c_i.
For every delta > 0, T_delta F_i lies strictly in the positive-time collar algebra A_{+,delta}. The regulated lattice or cell theory gives Q_{a,L}(T_delta F,c) >= 0 by reflection positivity.

Use the cutoff-removal topology on fixed-collar reflected probes to pass to the continuum: Q_S(T_delta F,c) = lim Q_{a,L}(T_delta F,c) >= 0. This step is valid precisely because the supports stay a positive distance from the reflection plane.

For the local-composite subcore, write each matrix entry as a finite sum of continuum distributions applied to translated test functions. Since f_delta -> f in C_c^infty, distributional continuity gives S(Theta T_delta F_i T_delta F_j) -> S(Theta F_i F_j). Hence the trace modulus holds for this subcore.

For the Wilson-loop part, reduce the same limit to two requirements: continuity of renormalized loop correlations under C^2 mirror-smooth deformation, and convergence of renormalization ratios Z_a(C_delta)/Z_a(C) to 1. If both hold, the same trace modulus follows.
Taking delta downarrow 0 in Q_S(T_delta F,c) >= 0 gives Q_S(F,c) >= 0. Density of A_+^{ms} in the OS seminorm then extends positivity to the full intended gauge-invariant algebra.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The hard algebra for Yang-Mills is not only local composites; gauge-invariant Wilson-type observables can develop cusp anomalous factors or contact terms as reflected supports collide. Without proving these are absent, the collar limit may be positive but for an altered boundary-renormalized theory.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: collar trace bridge

assumptions: For every fixed delta > 0 and every finite family F_i in A_+^{ms}, the RG cutoff-removal topology is strong enough to pass the regulated inequality Q_{a,L}(T_delta F,c) >= 0 to Q_S(T_delta F,c) >= 0.
Trace modulus: for every finite family F_i in A_+^{ms} there exists omega_F(delta) -> 0 such that |Q_S(T_delta F,c) - Q_S(F,c)| <= omega_F(delta) sum_i |c_i|^2 for all coefficient vectors c.
The same reflection Theta acts before and after cutoff removal under the chosen embeddings; in particular, no gauge fixing, quotienting, or boundary projection changes the test algebra.
A_+^{ms} is dense in the intended OS seminorm after quotienting null vectors, and the density is implemented by the same continuum Schwinger functional S rather than by adding boundary observables.
The finite matrices with entries S(Theta T_delta F_i T_delta F_j) have finite limits as delta downarrow 0.
definitions: source object: a cutoff net of reflection-positive gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals S_{a,L} on lattice/cell observables, together with embeddings iota_{a,L} of a fixed continuum positive-time core into the regulated observable algebra.

target object: an OS-positive continuum Schwinger functional S on the locked gauge-invariant positive-time algebra A_+, from which the OS Hilbert space, vacuum, and positive time-translation semigroup can be reconstructed.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions by first passing positivity at positive distance delta from the reflection plane, then proving a trace limit as delta downarrow 0.

same-theory condition: the maps iota_{a,L}, the collar maps T_delta, and the continuum inclusion of the mirror-smooth core into A_+ commute in the limit and introduce no reflection-plane counterterm, no changed Wilson-loop renormalization, and no quotient/enlargement of the gauge-invariant algebra.
A_{+,delta} is the subalgebra generated by gauge-invariant observables whose Euclidean supports have time-coordinate at least delta > 0.

A_+^{ms} is a mirror-smooth positive-time core: local renormalized gauge-invariant composites are smeared by C_c^infty functions supported in t >= 0 and flat at t = 0, and loop/cylinder observables have doubled reflected contours with no corner at the reflection plane.
T_delta: A_+^{ms} -> A_{+,delta} is a collaring operation, e.g. normal translation/smoothing into t >= delta, chosen so T_delta F converges to F in the core topology as delta downarrow 0.
Q_S(F,c) denotes the finite OS quadratic form sum_{i,j} conjugate(c_i)c_j S(Theta F_i F_j), where F_i are positive-time gauge-invariant observables.

equations.label: fixed-collar positivity
equations.valid_when: Valid after cutoff removal for each fixed delta > 0, provided RG convergence controls the reflected collar probes.

equations.label: trace modulus
equations.valid_when: Valid when the continuum Schwinger distributions have a boundary trace on the chosen mirror-smooth core and no reflection-plane anomaly is present.

equations.label: collar limit
equations.valid_when: Valid once both fixed-collar positivity and the trace modulus hold for the same finite family F_i and coefficients c_i.

equations.label: boundary-defect falsifier
equations.valid_when: This is the obstruction form; if B_partial is nonzero and not part of the original observable definition, the bridge proves positivity only after changing the theory.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Try a family of Wilson loops whose reflected double develops a cusp or a curvature contact term at t = 0. If the collar limit produces a nonzero B_partial or a new multiplicative cusp factor, that is a falsifier of the same-theory bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the only non-formal step after the closed-cone argument: a valid trace theorem converts fixed-collar OS positivity into full OS positivity while preserving the same gauge-invariant theory.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Collar-to-plane OS positivity lemma. Let S be the continuum gauge-invariant Schwinger functional obtained as the cutoff limit. Suppose fixed-collar reflected quadratic forms are nonnegative, and suppose every finite reflected quadratic form on a mirror-smooth positive-time core has a trace modulus as the collar is collapsed to the reflection plane. Then S is OS-positive on that core. If the core is OS-norm dense in the intended gauge-invariant positive-time algebra with no boundary renormalization, then S is OS-positive for the same continuum Yang-Mills theory, not for an enlarged boundary theory.

assumptions: All Schwinger distributions involving the chosen local composites are continuous multilinear functionals on the relevant test-function spaces.
Translation f -> f_delta is continuous in the test-function topology as delta downarrow 0.
Renormalization of the local composites is bulk renormalization only; no term supported on the reflection plane is introduced by the collaring operation.
definitions: Let O_alpha be renormalized gauge-invariant local composite fields such as tr F_{mu nu}F_{mu nu} or smeared curvature polynomials.
Let f_alpha in C_c^infty(R^4) have support in t >= 0 and be flat at t = 0; define f_{alpha,delta}(t,x)=f_alpha(t-delta,x).
The local core consists of finite polynomials in O_alpha(f_alpha), with gauge-invariant Wick/renormalized products interpreted through the continuum Schwinger distributions.

equations.label: test-function translation continuity
equations.valid_when: Valid for smooth functions supported in t >= 0 and flat at t = 0, after choosing delta small enough that supports remain in a fixed compact set.

equations.label: distributional trace for local composites
equations.valid_when: Valid when S_n is a genuine distribution on the composite-field test space and not merely a limit defined away from coincident/reflection-plane configurations.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed continuum construction defines composite Schwinger functions only for separated supports and lacks extension to test functions touching t = 0, the sublemma cannot be applied.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Provides a provable model case showing that the trace problem is not vacuous; it is solved for flat local smearing but remains hard for Wilson-loop and nonlocal gauge-invariant probes.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the subcore generated only by renormalized local gauge-invariant composite fields smeared with smooth positive-time test functions flat at the reflection plane, the trace modulus follows from ordinary distributional continuity of the continuum Schwinger distributions, assuming these composites have already been constructed as finite distributions.

assumptions: The loop observables under consideration are genuine elements, or OS-limits of elements, of the chosen gauge-invariant test algebra.
Renormalized loop correlations are continuous for mirror-smooth C^2 deformations that do not create bulk cusps or self-intersections.
The ratio between the renormalization assigned to C_delta and that assigned to C tends to 1 as delta downarrow 0, uniformly along the cutoff-removal subnet used to define S.
definitions: Let C_delta be the collar deformation of a mirror-smooth contour C, with C_delta contained in t >= delta and C_delta -> C in C^2 loop topology.
Let W_R(C) be the renormalized gauge-invariant Wilson observable assigned to C in the intended continuum theory.
A boundary factor is a multiplicative or additive renormalization depending on intersections, tangencies, or curvatures at the reflection plane rather than on the intrinsic bulk contour data.

equations.label: loop continuity target
equations.valid_when: Valid only if renormalized Wilson correlations are continuous in loop space at mirror-smooth boundary-touching contours.

equations.label: renormalization-ratio same-theory test
equations.valid_when: Valid when the same bulk Wilson-loop renormalization defines both the collar approximants and the boundary-touching observable.

equations.label: cusp-anomaly obstruction
equations.valid_when: This is a falsifier scenario: a nontrivial cusp or boundary anomalous factor means the collar bridge changes the observable normalization.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Construct a reflected loop family whose doubled contour has a limiting angle theta at the plane; a nontrivial cusp anomalous dimension would block same-theory OS positivity for the loop algebra.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the vague phrase no boundary counterterm into a measurable condition on loop renormalization constants and loop-space continuity.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For Wilson-loop or loop-cylinder observables, the collar trace is a same-theory statement if the renormalized loop Schwinger functions are continuous under mirror-smooth C^2 deformations to the reflection plane and their renormalization constants have no additional boundary-local factor. This criterion converts the Wilson-loop part of OS positivity into a concrete renormalization-ratio test.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a Wilson-loop cusp or boundary-contact falsifier is exhibited, or if RG convergence cannot even provide distributional continuity for flat local composite smearing at t = 0.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves no-boundary-renormalization for mirror-smooth loop observables and OS-density of the mirror-smooth core in the intended gauge-invariant algebra.
control_decision.reason: The branch is still producing sharper proof obligations: it has reduced the trace modulus to a provable local-core sublemma plus a concrete loop renormalization-ratio test.

dependency_updates.description: Split into a formal fixed-collar closed-cone step and a nonformal collar-to-plane trace theorem. The former is valid under RG domination of reflected probes; the latter is now the main analytic obligation.

Proposed A_+^{ms}: local smooth flat-at-boundary composites plus mirror-smooth loop observables. The local part has a plausible trace proof; the loop part requires a no-boundary-renormalization criterion.
The topology must dominate fixed-collar OS quadratic forms and also provide continuity under test-function translation and mirror-smooth loop deformation as delta downarrow 0.
Need to prove that collar collapse introduces no boundary-local counterterm, cusp anomalous factor, or changed Wilson-loop normalization. This is the same-theory certificate.

falsifiers: A concrete falsifier would be a mirror-smooth loop family C_delta whose continuum Wilson-loop correlation has a nontrivial limiting cusp or boundary anomalous factor, so that Z_a(C_delta)/Z_a(C) does not tend to 1.

If the RG compactness topology controls only observables separated from t = 0 and gives no distributional extension to test functions flat at the reflection plane, then even the local-core trace modulus is not valid.

If the positive-time test algebra after cutoff removal includes boundary observables or removes null states differently from the regulated gauge-invariant algebra, fixed-collar positivity does not certify OS positivity for the same theory.

If curvature-contact terms supported at the reflection plane appear in limits of S(Theta T_delta F_i T_delta F_j), then the limiting quadratic form is Q_S plus a boundary defect B_partial, not the desired Q_S.
If Wilson loops are not continuous under the needed C^2 collar deformation, the closed-cone argument remains formally true but applies only to a smaller collar algebra.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 176 separates the trace problem into a solved model piece and a genuine Yang-Mills obstruction. For local gauge-invariant composites smeared by smooth functions flat at the reflection plane, the collar trace is just distributional continuity, so OS positivity can be extended there by a valid limiting argument. The difficult part is therefore not the closed cone and not all boundary contact in general; it is specifically the Wilson-loop/nonlocal sector, where collar collapse can create cusp factors or boundary renormalizations. The branch has learned a sharper falsifier: find a nontrivial renormalization ratio Z_a(C_delta)/Z_a(C) in a reflected loop family, and the same-theory OS bridge fails.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out an explicit reflected rectangular or rounded Wilson-loop collar family C_delta, compute the expected perimeter/cusp/curvature renormalization ratio symbolically, and identify whether mirror-smooth rounding eliminates all boundary-local anomalous factors or merely hides them in Z_a(C_delta).
